title: Kiosk account binding -- claim and link
description: The wire objects of Section 6, the one-time ceremonies that bind a registered AI assistant to an existing operator account: claim, an RFC 8628 device grant, and link. Both need the human's approval and a client assertion by the registered key. The two /oauth/* requests are form-encoded and have no schema here; their answers are in auth.schema.json.

deviceAuthorization.description: Section 6.1 step 1: the answer to POST <endpoint>/oauth/device_authorization. All six members are required, also the two that RFC 8628 makes optional.

device_code.description: The opaque code the AI assistant polls with. Never shown to the human.

user_code.description: The short code the human types at the verification page.

verification_uri.description: The operator's session-authenticated approval page (Section 15.8), which names the access the approval hands over.

verification_uri_complete.description: The same page with the `user_code` already carried, so the human does not have to type it.

interval.description: Seconds the AI assistant waits between polls. A poll that arrives sooner may be answered `slow_down`.

deviceTokenResponse.description: Section 6.1 step 3: the success answer to the device-code poll of POST <endpoint>/oauth/token. `scope` is the approving human's role.

oauthError.description: Section 6.1: the error answer of both /oauth/* endpoints, the one error shape on this wire that is not an RFC 9457 problem document.

linkCode.description: Section 6.2 -- the 201 answer to POST <endpoint>/auth/link, called on the operator's own session by the signed-in human. 201 rather than 200 because the call MINTS a redeemable single-use credential.

link_code.description: A long opaque token, paste-grade -- the human hands it to their AI assistant. Stored hashed, single-use, short-TTL and attempt-capped (Section 6.3).

expires_in.description: Seconds until the link code expires.

claimRequest.description: Section 6.2 -- the body of POST <endpoint>/auth/claim, which redeems a link code. The client assertion is REQUIRED, so a leaked code alone can never bind a key its holder does not control. The answer is 204 No Content; the AI assistant then asks the token endpoint for a token under the human's account.

client_assertion.description: A client assertion by the registered key (auth.schema.json#/$defs/clientAssertion).

unlinkRequest.description: Section 6.3 -- the body of POST <endpoint>/auth/unlink, called on the operator's own session. The response is 204 No Content and carries no body at all, which is why no response object appears here.

agent_id.description: The bound AI assistant (its client_id) to deactivate. Its tokens stop verifying and the token endpoint answers it `invalid_client` (Section 15.4).
